comparisons.peer_topic: Estimates and Assumptions in Asset Valuation
comparisons.peer_summary: Management makes significant estimates and assumptions to determine fair values, particularly for intangible assets, including revenue growth rates, margins, technology changes, customer relationship timelines, useful lives, and discount rates. These fair value estimates reflect market participant assumptions but are inherently uncertain, meaning actual results may differ.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose their methodologies for valuing acquired intangible assets, specifically highlighting the use of estimates and assumptions regarding customer relationships and revenue. AVGO explicitly details the 'with-and-without method' under the income approach to value customer contracts, relying on factors like 'historical customer turnover rates.' AMD similarly identifies 'time to recreate customer relationships' and 'expected future revenue growth rates' as critical estimates in valuing intangible assets, noting that these fair value estimates reflect market participant assumptions but are inherently uncertain.

sentences.text: Customer contracts and related relationships represent the fair value of future projected revenue that will be derived from sales of products to existing customers of VMware.

In the with-and-without method, the fair value was measured by the difference between the present values of the cash flows with and without the existing customers in place over the period of time necessary to reacquire the customers.

The economic useful life was determined by evaluating many factors, including the useful life of other intangible assets, the length of time remaining on the acquired contracts and the historical customer turnover rates.
When determining the fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed, management makes significant estimates and assumptions, especially with respect to intangible assets.

Critical estimates in valuing intangible assets include, but are not limited to, expected future revenue growth rates and margins, future changes in technology, time to recreate customer relationships, useful lives, and discount rates.
Fair value estimates are based on the assumptions that management believes a market participant would use in pricing the asset or liability.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intangible Assets Composition and Amortization Policy
comparisons.peer_summary: Intangible assets primarily represent acquired developed technology, customer relationships, and licensed IP, which are amortized over periods ranging from one to twenty years using methods that reflect economic benefit consumption or straight-line if the pattern cannot be determined.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA identify 'customer relationships' as a key component of their acquired intangible assets. AVGO states that customer contracts represent the fair value of future revenue from existing VMware customers. NVDA similarly notes that its intangible assets primarily include 'customer relationships' alongside developed technology and licensed IP. While AVGO provides specific valuation mechanics (with-and-without method) and NVDA provides amortization policies (1-20 years), both disclosures confirm that customer-related intangibles are significant acquired assets valued based on future economic benefits.

sentences.text: Customer contracts and related relationships represent the fair value of future projected revenue that will be derived from sales of products to existing customers of VMware.
Customer contracts and related relationships were valued using the with-and-without-method under the income approach.

Intangible assets primarily represent acquired intangible assets including developed technology and customer relationships, as well as rights acquired under technology licenses, patents, and acquired IP.

We currently amortize our intangible assets with finite lives over periods ranging from one to twenty years using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits of the intangible asset are consumed or otherwise used up or, if that pattern cannot be reliably determined, using a straight-line amortization method.

comparisons.peer_summary: Quantitative impairment tests estimate fair value using income and market approaches, requiring assumptions about prospective financials, growth rates, discount rates, and other economic factors.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures involve fair value estimation techniques for business combinations. AVGO uses the 'income approach' (with-and-without method) to value specific intangible assets (customer contracts) by comparing cash flow present values. NVDA describes using both 'income approach and the market approach' for quantitative goodwill impairment tests, noting that these approaches require assumptions about prospective financials and discount rates. Both companies rely on discounted cash flow concepts inherent in income-based valuation methodologies to determine fair value, though they apply them to different asset classes (specific intangibles vs. reporting unit goodwill).

sentences.text: Customer contracts and related relationships were valued using the with-and-without-method under the income approach.

In the with-and-without method, the fair value was measured by the difference between the present values of the cash flows with and without the existing customers in place over the period of time necessary to reacquire the customers.
The quantitative impairment test considers both the income approach and the market approach to estimate a reporting unit's fair value.

The income and market valuation approaches consider factors that include, but are not limited to, prospective financial information, growth rates, residual values, discount rates and comparable multiples from publicly traded companies in our industry and require us to make certain assumptions and estimates regarding industry economic factors and the future profitability of our business.
